In this tutorial you will build a titin doublet from two `Spheroid` subunits
and three `GaussianPolymer` chains. You will use `World.Link` to connect them,
`EvaluateFormFactor` to calculate their scattering, and `visualize` to inspect
the fitted dimensions.

The question is simple: **does a good fit also give a sensible linker size?**

::: {.callout-note title="Before you start"}
Work through [Your first composite model](diblock-copolymer.qmd) first.
For the SciPy fitting pattern, see [Fit the corona to F127 data](fit-f127-data.qmd).
Here we concentrate on the pySEB model supplied to the optimizer.
:::

This four-page sequence reuses the same SAXS data and connected topology:

| Page | What you will do in pySEB |
| --- | --- |
| **1. This page** | Connect analytical subunits and evaluate a parameter dictionary |
| [2. Coordinate domains](titin-coordinate-domains.qmd) | Build coordinate clouds with named terminal references |
| [3. Atomic scattering and hydration](titin-hydration.qmd) | Configure atomic scattering and solvent options |
| [4. Relative scattering weights](titin-relative-weights.qmd) | Change subunit amplitudes through `beta` parameters |

## Prepare your environment

Use a pySEB installation with the `visualization` extra enabled. The worked
example also uses NumPy, Matplotlib, IPython, and SciPy:

```bash
python -m pip install numpy scipy matplotlib plotly usd-core ipython
```

Run the page from `docs/tutorials` in a repository checkout. The website loads
saved fits so you can explore the model without waiting for optimization.
The complete calculation source is expandable at the end of each page;
[one command](#reproduce-the-saved-calculations) runs all four stages.

{{< include _titin-setup.qmd >}}

## 1. Connect the five subunits

Our construct has an N-terminal tail, two folded I27 domains, an eight-residue
linker, and a C-terminal tail:

```text
N-tail — domain 1 — linker — domain 2 — C-tail
```

Start a `World`, add the first spheroid, and extend its graph with `Link`.
Each link names one reference on the new subunit and one on the existing graph.
For example, `linker.end1` meets `domain1.north`.

```{python}
#| code-fold: false
world = pyseb.World("TitinTutorial")
graph = world.Add("Spheroid", "domain1")
world.Link("GaussianPolymer", "ntail.end2", "domain1.south")
world.Link("GaussianPolymer", "linker.end1", "domain1.north")
world.Link("Spheroid", "domain2.south", "linker.end2")
world.Link("GaussianPolymer", "ctail.end1", "domain2.north")
_ = world.Add(graph, "titin")
```
The final `Add` names the assembled graph `titin`. Use that name when
evaluating or displaying the whole structure. Both domains use the same
spheroid dimensions, but they remain distinct instances with their own links.

## 2. Supply dimensions and scattering weights

pySEB separates topology from parameter values. The same `world` can be reused
with different dimensions by passing a new dictionary to the evaluator.
Here we start with the saved constrained fit:

```{python}
#| code-fold: false
a, c, linker_rg, tail_rg8 = results["fits"]["analytical_constrained"]["x"][:4]
parameters = {
    "Rg_linker": linker_rg, "beta_linker": 8.0,
    "Rg_ntail": tail_rg8 * np.sqrt(24.0 / 8.0), "beta_ntail": 24.0,
    "Rg_ctail": tail_rg8 * np.sqrt(7.0 / 8.0), "beta_ctail": 7.0,
}
for name in ("domain1", "domain2"):
    parameters.update({
        f"a_{name}": a, f"c_{name}": c, f"beta_{name}": 89.0,
    })
```
The suffix selects the subunit instance: `Rg_linker` changes the linker,
while `a_domain1` changes domain 1. The `beta` values set relative scattering
amplitudes. For now, use residue counts: **24:89:8:89:7**. Page 4 will test
this assumption.

Both terminal tails share a chain-size parameter, `tail_rg8`, scaled by the
square root of residue count. The central linker has its own independent
`Rg_linker`. Lengths are in ångströms throughout this example.

## 3. Evaluate the connected model

Pass the structure name, parameter dictionary, and q values to
`EvaluateFormFactor`. pySEB includes scattering from each part and the
interference between connected parts:

```{python}
#| code-fold: false
form_factor = np.asarray(
    world.EvaluateFormFactor("titin", parameters, q.tolist())
)
scale, background = results["fits"]["analytical_constrained"]["x"][4:]
model_intensity = scale * form_factor + background
compare_curves({"Constrained analytical model": model_intensity})
```
The normalized form factor has $P(0)=1$. To compare it with the measurement,
we use $I(q)=S P(q)+B$, with fitted scale $S$ and flat background $B$.
SciPy varies the parameter values; pySEB evaluates the connected structure.
The full fit uses six variables: two shared spheroid semi-axes, linker size,
terminal-chain size, scale, and background.

The measurement is [SASBDB SASDKC2](https://www.sasbdb.org/data/SASDKC2/).
The local curve retains every fourth deposited point through
$q=0.30\;\mathrm{\AA}^{-1}$. The optimizer uses alternating local points;
the remaining points provide a held-point check. The score on those nearby
points is a diagnostic, not independent experimental validation.

## 4. Inspect the linker before accepting the fit

First allow $0.5 \le R_{g,\mathrm{linker}} \le 9$ Å. The saved diagnostic fit
looks convincing by its score:

```{python}
#| echo: false
fit_table("analytical_collapsed")
```
But the linker reaches its **0.5 Å lower bound**. For a Gaussian polymer,
the RMS end-to-end distance is $\sqrt{6}R_g$, only about 1.2 Å here.
That is an implausibly small ensemble size for an eight-residue peptide.
The adjustable domain shapes and chain dimensions are compensating for one another.

Refit with a broad working constraint of **4–9 Å**. An ideal chain with eight
3.8 Å steps gives $R_g \approx 4.4$ Å, which motivates the scale without
establishing exact bounds for a short peptide.

```{python}
#| echo: false
fit_table("analytical_constrained")
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
compare_curves({
    "Weak bound: Rg >= 0.5 A": curves["analytical_collapsed"],
    "Physical working bound: Rg >= 4 A": curves["analytical_constrained"],
})
```
The training reduced chi-squared changes from about **1.34 to 1.44**, while
the linker moves to the new **4 Å lower bound**. The curve changes little;
the bound supplies physical information that this fit does not identify by itself.

## 5. View the model and try another linker size

Use the same `world` and `parameters` with `pyseb.visualize`:

```{python}
#| code-fold: false
options = pyseb.USDExportOptions(pyseb.LengthUnit.Angstrom)
options.seed = 42
_ = pyseb.visualize(
    world, "titin", parameters, options, height=440,
    layouts=["random", "readable"],
)
```
Rotate the view and switch between layouts. The chains show illustrative
realizations of an ensemble model; the scattering data do not recover one
unique conformation. The readable layout adjusts the display orientations.
It does not add excluded volume to the Gaussian-chain calculation.

**Try it:** change only the linker size and reuse the assembled graph.
Keep scale and background fixed so you can see the direct effect:

```{python}
#| code-fold: false
trial_curves = {}
for trial_rg in (0.5, 4.0, 9.0):
    trial_parameters = {**parameters, "Rg_linker": trial_rg}
    trial_p = np.asarray(world.EvaluateFormFactor(
        "titin", trial_parameters, q.tolist()))
    trial_curves[f"Linker Rg = {trial_rg:g} Å; no refit"] = scale * trial_p + background
compare_curves(trial_curves)
```
Which q range responds most to the change? These curves are a parameter
sweep, so they need not match fits in which all six variables were reoptimized.

## Continue

You can now connect analytical subunits, pass dimensions and amplitudes to
the evaluator, and inspect the resulting model. Next,
[replace the spheroids with coordinate domains](titin-coordinate-domains.qmd)
while retaining the analytical linker and tails.

three pages in order. It saves curves, fit parameters, and OpenUSD scenes under

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Complete calculation source: analytical fits and scene export"}

These are the complete calculation cells used by the sequence generator.
They run in sequence order across the four pages; fitting and export cells
are disabled during website rendering. The short examples above can be run
after this page's setup without regenerating the fits.

```{python}
#| tags: [titin-generation]
#| eval: false
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pyseb
from IPython.display import Markdown, display
from scipy.interpolate import CubicSpline
from scipy.optimize import least_squares


data_directory = Path("data")
q, intensity, uncertainty = np.loadtxt(
    data_directory / "SASDKC2-titin.csv",
    delimiter=",",
    skiprows=3,
    unpack=True,
)

fit_q = q[::2]
fit_intensity = intensity[::2]
fit_uncertainty = uncertainty[::2]
held_q = q[1::2]
held_intensity = intensity[1::2]
held_uncertainty = uncertainty[1::2]

print(f"Stored points: {q.size}")
print(f"Points used by the optimizer: {fit_q.size}")
print(f"Alternating points held out: {held_q.size}")
print(f"q range: {q.min():.4f}--{q.max():.4f} A^-1")
```

```{python}
#| tags: [titin-generation]
n_tail_sequence = "MHHHHHHDYDIPTTENLYLQGGGG"
linker_sequence = "GGGSGGGG"
c_tail_sequence = "LPETGSS"
domain_beta = 89.0
linker_beta = float(len(linker_sequence))
n_tail_beta = float(len(n_tail_sequence))
c_tail_beta = float(len(c_tail_sequence))
diagnostic_linker_bounds = (0.5, 9.0)


def construct_tail_parameters(tail_rg8):
    return {
        "Rg_ntail": tail_rg8
        * np.sqrt(n_tail_beta / linker_beta),
        "beta_ntail": n_tail_beta,
        "Rg_ctail": tail_rg8
        * np.sqrt(c_tail_beta / linker_beta),
        "beta_ctail": c_tail_beta,
    }


def construct_polymer_parameters(linker_rg, tail_rg8):
    parameters = construct_tail_parameters(tail_rg8)
    parameters.update({
        "Rg_linker": linker_rg,
        "beta_linker": linker_beta,
    })
    return parameters


def print_derived_tail_radii(tail_rg8):
    parameters = construct_tail_parameters(tail_rg8)
    print(f"derived N-tail Rg [A]         = {parameters['Rg_ntail']:.6g}")
    print(f"derived C-tail Rg [A]         = {parameters['Rg_ctail']:.6g}")


def reduced_chi_squared(residual, number_of_parameters):
    degrees_of_freedom = residual.size - number_of_parameters
    return np.sum(residual**2) / degrees_of_freedom
```

```{python}
#| tags: [titin-generation]
#| eval: false
spheroid_world = pyseb.World("TitinSpheroids")
spheroid_graph = spheroid_world.Add("Spheroid", "domain1")
spheroid_world.Link(
    "GaussianPolymer",
    "ntail.end2",
    "domain1.south",
)
spheroid_world.Link(
    "GaussianPolymer",
    "linker.end1",
    "domain1.north",
)
spheroid_world.Link(
    "Spheroid",
    "domain2.south",
    "linker.end2",
)
spheroid_world.Link(
    "GaussianPolymer",
    "ctail.end1",
    "domain2.north",
)
spheroid_world.Add(spheroid_graph, "titin")

print("N-tail -- Spheroid -- linker -- Spheroid -- C-tail")
print("ntail.end2 = domain1.south")
print("domain1.north = linker.end1")
print("linker.end2 = domain2.south")
print("domain2.north = ctail.end1")
```

```{python}
#| tags: [titin-generation]
#| eval: false
def spheroid_curve(values, q_values):
    (
        equatorial_radius,
        polar_radius,
        linker_rg,
        tail_rg8,
        scale,
        background,
    ) = values
    parameters = construct_polymer_parameters(linker_rg, tail_rg8)
    parameters.update({
        "a_domain1": equatorial_radius,
        "c_domain1": polar_radius,
        "beta_domain1": domain_beta,
        "a_domain2": equatorial_radius,
        "c_domain2": polar_radius,
        "beta_domain2": domain_beta,
    })
    form_factor = np.asarray(
        spheroid_world.EvaluateFormFactor(
            "titin", parameters, q_values.tolist()
        )
    )
    return scale * form_factor + background


def spheroid_residual(values):
    return (
        spheroid_curve(values, fit_q) - fit_intensity
    ) / fit_uncertainty


unconstrained_fit = least_squares(
    spheroid_residual,
    x0=[14.0, 22.0, 5.0, 5.0, 0.033, 0.0002],
    bounds=(
        [5.0, 10.0, diagnostic_linker_bounds[0], 0.1, 0.0, 0.0],
        [30.0, 50.0, diagnostic_linker_bounds[1], 30.0, 1.0, 0.01],
    ),
    x_scale="jac",
)

spheroid_names = ["equatorial a [A]", "polar c [A]", "linker Rg [A]",
                  "tail Rg8 [A]", "scale", "background"]
for name, value in zip(spheroid_names, unconstrained_fit.x):
    print(f"{name:24s} = {value:.6g}")
print("Reduced chi-squared:",
      reduced_chi_squared(unconstrained_fit.fun, 6))
```

```{python}
#| tags: [titin-generation]
#| eval: false
print(f"Linker Rg = {unconstrained_fit.x[2]:.3f} A")
print(f"RMS end-to-end distance = {np.sqrt(6)*unconstrained_fit.x[2]:.3f} A")
```

```{python}
#| tags: [titin-generation]
#| eval: false
linker_rg_bounds = (4.0, 9.0)
spheroid_fit = least_squares(
    spheroid_residual,
    x0=[14.0, 22.0, 5.0, 5.0, 0.033, 0.0002],
    bounds=([5.0, 10.0, 4.0, 0.1, 0.0, 0.0],
            [30.0, 50.0, 9.0, 30.0, 1.0, 0.01]),
    x_scale="jac",
)
for name, value in zip(spheroid_names, spheroid_fit.x):
    print(f"{name:24s} = {value:.6g}")
print_derived_tail_radii(spheroid_fit.x[3])
print("Reduced chi-squared:", reduced_chi_squared(spheroid_fit.fun, 6))
```

```{python}
#| tags: [titin-generation]
def compare_curves(curves):
    figure, (axis, residual_axis) = plt.subplots(
        2, 1, figsize=(8, 6), sharex=True,
        gridspec_kw={"height_ratios": [3, 1]})
    axis.errorbar(q, intensity, uncertainty, fmt=".", color="black",
                  alpha=0.5, label="SASDKC2")
    for label, curve in curves.items():
        axis.plot(q, curve, label=label)
        residual_axis.plot(q, (curve-intensity)/uncertainty)
    axis.set(yscale="log", ylabel="Intensity [a.u.]")
    axis.legend(fontsize="small")
    residual_axis.axhline(0, color="gray", linewidth=1)
    residual_axis.set(xlabel=r"$q$ [$\mathrm{\AA}^{-1}$]",
                      ylabel=r"$(I_\mathrm{model}-I)/\sigma$")
    figure.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

```

```{python}

})

#| tags: [titin-generation]

visual_directory = data_directory / "titin-results" / "scenes"
visual_directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)


def show_structure(world, parameters, name):
    options = pyseb.USDExportOptions(pyseb.LengthUnit.Angstrom)
    options.seed = 42
    options.layout_mode = pyseb.LayoutMode.Readable
    options.orientation_trials = 32
    options.relaxation_sweeps = 2
    options.zero_radius_marker_size = 0.8
    options.color_overrides = {
        "domain1": (0.10, 0.55, 0.78), "domain2": (0.92, 0.43, 0.12),
        "linker": (0.2, 0.7, 0.3), "ntail": (0.6, 0.6, 0.6),
        "ctail": (0.6, 0.6, 0.6),
    }
    path = visual_directory / f"{name}.usda"
    world.export_usd("titin", str(path), parameters, options)
    _ = pyseb.visualize(world, "titin", parameters, options, height=440, layouts=["random", "readable"])
```

```{python}
#| tags: [titin-generation]
#| eval: false
def spheroid_parameters(values):
    a, c, linker_rg, tail_rg8 = values[:4]
    parameters = construct_polymer_parameters(linker_rg, tail_rg8)
    for domain in ("domain1", "domain2"):
        parameters.update({f"a_{domain}": a, f"c_{domain}": c,
                           f"beta_{domain}": domain_beta})
    return parameters

show_structure(spheroid_world, spheroid_parameters(unconstrained_fit.x),
               "analytical-collapsed")
show_structure(spheroid_world, spheroid_parameters(spheroid_fit.x),
               "analytical-constrained")
```
